description: We are a team based in Seattle, USA interested in learning more about how microgravity affects flames!
summary: Ignis_0G is an interactive web dashboard that turns NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion records into fire safety insights for crewed environments in space. We collected 24 relevant PSI investigations (19 from flight experiments and 5 from ground studies) and gave each one an overview page. The overview page lists key conditions and builds graphs from the investigation's data, and also has links back to the PSI record. Additionally, a browser simulation allows users to change variables such as oxygen concentration and airflow to test different conditions. With Ignis AI, users ask a question and the assistant ranks the investigations by relevance to the scenario, and pulls specific information from PSI records to answer questions along with its own analysis of the data. A big issue that we noticed was that fire behaves differently in microgravity, so our dashboard helps researchers find the relevant evidence quickly for their work.
details:
Ignis_0G is a web dashboard that helps researches quickly find and use NASA combustion research and other relevant sources for fire safety. Our features include:

Simulation: Researchers can use this project to get preliminary fire-safety estimates across a range of gravity conditions, including microgravity, which is a condition that has not been studied in depth.

Investigations: It builds preliminary figures from the dataset itself and also sets them in comparison with official PSI investigation pages. This allows researchers to skim across datasets and determine which one suits their needs the best. Every single figure and dataset has links and citations back to its original source.

Ignis AI: The AI is grounded in our 24 investigations that we hand-picked for this challenge, and can rank them by relevancy based on a question or sentence stem. The same AI is built into the dashboard as a support bot, so users can ask relevant questions anytime and get an answer backed with sources.

Our work mainly includes the 24 PSI investigations that are cited first in our sources, but it also draws on over 350+ NASA and Space Agency publications. Our dashboard is built with JavaScript, React, Vite, and Plotly.js, and we integrated gpt-oss-120b through Groq as Ignis AI. SI supported the development of our dashboard through coding and analysis, but all work was reviewed and checked thoroughly by humans before merging with main.

However, due to the range of PSI data, our simulation doesn't cover lunar or Martian gravity yet. Therefore, it only can provide estimates, not validated predictions. Access to a larger number of data points across a range of different conditions would help to make our fire safety scenarios more accurate. Ignis AI also faces token limits, so very long or rapid inquiries may be cut off. In the future, we plan to add more partial gravity data as it comes out to grow the dataset and simulation, and invest additional capital into Ignis AI to increase its capabilities.
